questions.question: Describe how to make a circle pillar, a triangle pillar and a square pillar from paper.
questions.expected_answer: For a circle pillar, roll the paper into a tube, overlap the edges and tape them. For a triangle pillar, fold the paper lengthways into three equal strips plus a flap and tape it. For a square pillar, fold it into four equal strips plus a flap and tape it. All should be the same height.

questions.question: Which pillar shape usually holds the most, and why?
questions.expected_answer: The circle pillar usually holds the most, because it has no corners or folds, so the load is shared evenly all the way around the paper. Square and triangle pillars carry the load mostly at their corners, and their flat sides buckle.

questions.question: What is a strut and how do you make one from paper?
questions.expected_answer: A strut is a stiff part of a structure that holds other parts up or apart. To make one, roll a sheet of paper tightly and diagonally around a thin stick, glue the last corner and slide the stick out.
